{{Short description|American organic chemist (1929–2013)}}
'''Herbert Otis House''' (December 5, 1929 – October 2, 2013<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.memorialsolutions.com/sitemaker/memsol.cgi?user_id=1117463|title=Obituary for Herbert House - Alpharetta, GA|website=www.memorialsolutions.com|access-date=2016-08-09}}</ref>) was an American organic chemist.

House was born in [[Willoughby, Ohio]]. He received a Bachelor of Science in chemistry from [[Miami University]] in Ohio in 1950 a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1953 from the University of Illinois under the guidance of [[Reynold C. Fuson|Reynold Fuson]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=53780|title=Chemistry Tree - Herbert O. House Details|website=academictree.org|access-date=2016-08-09}}</ref> Upon graduation, he joined the faculty of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and remained there until 1970. During this time, he co-discovered the [[Corey–House synthesis|Corey-House alkane synthesis]], an early example of a transition metal mediated cross-coupling reaction. In 1970, he joined the faculty of the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]]. House retired in 1990 and was the Vasser Woolley Professor Emeritus at Georgia Tech until his death in 2013 in [[Alpharetta, Georgia]].

In addition to the publication of 180 scientific papers, House received the [[American Chemical Society]]'s Award for Creative Work in Synthetic Chemistry (1975) and authored the textbook ''Modern Synthetic Reactions''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/92/i6/Herbert-O-House.html|title=Herbert O. House {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|last=Ainsworth|first=Susan J.|website=cen.acs.org|access-date=2016-08-10}}</ref> Renowned organic chemist [[Barry Trost]] (Stanford University, formerly Wisconsin) received his Ph.D. (1965) under his mentorship.
